Goldman restricts traders and bankers from using some AI tools — Bloomberg
article:
(Nov 2): Goldman Sachs Group Inc has irked some of its staff after it banned most of them from using advanced artificial intelligence (AI) tools designed for coding after reviewing productivity and risk concerns.

For months, Goldman allowed bankers to use Anthropic PBC’s Claude Code and Microsoft Corp’s GitHub for work. Now, the bank is limiting the use of those tools to engineers only, according to internal guidance updated in October and seen by Bloomberg News.

The ban has frustrated some traders, who had used the tools to accelerate aspects of their work such as monitoring client trading flows, modelling market changes and positions, and creating written and graphic content, according to a person familiar with the matter, who asked not to be identified talking about private information.

As recently as July, Goldman chief information officer Marco Argenti touted the “vibe coding” by non-technical employees at Goldman, such as traders and bankers. Those staff members had developed solutions with AI tools and passed on their creations to one of the firm’s 12,000 engineers to improve, he said in an interview.

Goldman Sachs chief information officer Marco Argenti at the Wave by Vento tech conference in Turin, Italy on Oct 9. (Photo by Bloomberg)

See also: US stock rotation hits AI winners on spending worries

“We make certain AI tools available to our people to determine the best use cases across different parts of the firm,” said Nick Carcaterra, a Goldman spokesperson. “After a period of experimentation where we assess a variety of factors including productivity and risk management, we put them in the hands of those who are best suited to leverage them for the long term.”

It’s the latest twist as Wall Street irons out just exactly how it wants its thousands of workers using AI models. Banks are spending millions of dollars on AI tools while also trying to figure out how to navigate the increasing concerns around cybersecurity risk, costs and productivity.

JPMorgan Chase & Co said in July that it was seeking to have employees figure out what model to use for what purpose, helping to avoid using the most expensive model for a task as simple as summarising an analyst report. Goldman itself has developed an AI assistant that combines models from OpenAI, Anthropic and Alphabet Inc.

See also: Tech stocks slide as Alphabet’s record plunge revives AI fears

At the same time, Wall Street firms are benefitting from the surging financing needs of AI firms. Goldman has been named lead underwriter on Anthropic’s blockbuster initial public offering and has partnered with chipmaker Nvidia Corp to arrange major debt deals.

In May, John Waldron, the heir apparent to chief executive officer David Solomon, said he viewed Goldman as a “human assembly line” that was ripe for automation.

It’s not the first time that the bank has pulled back on allowing employees to use certain AI tools. Earlier this year, the bank restricted the use of Anthropic’s Claude by its staff in Hong Kong, a location-specific restriction.

The bank’s latest directive doesn’t apply to so-called “strats,” employees who sit at the intersection of trading, quantitative research and software engineering, said another person.

title: China to expand stock support tools to stabilise market
article:
(Nov 2): China will encourage financial institutions to make fuller use of two stock support tools and optimise their terms, as authorities step up efforts to bolster market stability and confidence.

The People’s Bank of China (PBOC) said it will conduct operations under its swap facility for securities firms, funds and insurers when appropriate. It will also increase the number of participating institutions and moderately lower swap fees, the central bank said in a statement on Monday following a meeting with financial regulators and institutions.

Separately, it will cut the rate on its relending facility for share buybacks and stake increases to 1% from 1.25%, make the programme permanent and encourage banks to increase lending, the PBOC said.

The two tools were introduced in October 2024 as Beijing sought to shore up the stock market. The relending facility provides low-cost central bank funding to banks for loans financing share buybacks and stake increases by listed companies and major shareholders.

The China Securities Regulatory Commission (CSRC) said in a separate statement that a third round of swap operations will begin in coming days, with 31 securities and fund firms approved to participate and applying for more than 100 billion yuan of quotas. The regulator also plans to broaden the coverage of the relending programme, including by encouraging more major index constituents and leading technology companies to participate.

The CSRC also plans to ease share buyback rules, including allowing companies to repurchase shares when their stock falls below the IPO price and requiring companies with excess fundraising proceeds to conduct buybacks when market support conditions are triggered. It will also study changes to margin-financing requirements to moderately increase financing capacity and improve market liquidity.

See also: Danone targets China’s ageing population with new research hub

Chinese shares have been mired in a slump since the summer amid a weak economy and doubts over artificial intelligence earnings. The CSI 300 Index fell 8.5% in October, its worst monthly decline in more than a decade, and dropped for a record 12 straight weeks through Friday.

About 440 billion yuan of loans supporting share buybacks and stake increases have been contracted, with more than 280 billion yuan disbursed, according to the central bank. The outstanding balance of the swap facility is 105 billion yuan.

The meeting was attended by 23 securities firms, funds and 26 banks. Representatives from China International Capital Corp, Guotai Haitong Securities Co, Citic Securities Co, Industrial & Commercial Bank of China Ltd, China Construction Bank Corp and China Citic Bank Corp were among those who spoke, the PBOC said.

title: Danone targets China’s ageing population with new research hub
article:
(Nov 2): Danone is ramping up research investment in China as it plans more medical nutrition products aimed at the country’s ageing population.

The French maker of protein-rich yogurts and fortified drinks opened a research and innovation center in Shanghai on Monday — its third so-called OneBiome Lab after France and Singapore — to focus on areas including gut bacteria.

“There is a big opportunity around healthy ageing and around our life support,” Chief executive officer Antoine de Saint-Affrique said in an interview, citing the company’s “strong science” in proteins that he said are essential for muscles and mobility. “At the heart of what we are doing is microbiota, which is at the origin of most diseases and which is a field where Danone was born.”

While Danone’s specialised nutrition products such as Aptamil infant formula are popular in China, it also knows its second-largest market accounting for 12% of global sales in 2025 is going through a profound demographic shift. Outside a baby boom in the Year of the Dragon in 2024, birth rates are plummeting, with just under eight million last year compared with about 17 million in 2017.

Meanwhile Chinese policymakers refer to a “silver economy” to describe an older generation that benefitted from globalisation, a two-decade real estate boom and rapid economic growth. About 360 million people in China, or roughly a quarter, were born during a population surge between 1962 and 1975.

See also: Chinese stock sell-off halts as support measures expected

Danone’s research aims to capture growing demand for maintaining mobility, managing microbiota, and supporting health through medical nutrition, Saint-Affrique said. It will also launch products at the China International Import Expo this week, he added, including a supplement for sustained weight management.

Saint-Affrique is five years into a turnaround of the French dairy group, based on offloading underperforming businesses and pushing its healthy food portfolio.

Demand for Danone’s high-protein yogurts has soared across markets amid a consumer craze for protein and gut health. The specialised nutrition business, which includes infant formula and hospital tube feeds, has generated less buzz but was its fastest-growing business in the latest quarter.

See also: China's main solar poducers post losses in latest quarter despite margin recovery

Danone last year acquired Kate Farms, which makes plant-based medical nutrition products for children, to help drive growth in the US, while the specialised nutrition market is also growing strongly in the Asia-Pacific.

Given the ageing population in many countries, Danone has been looking to expand beyond specialised tube-feeding products used into hospitals into more over-the-counter items to be sold at pharmacies.

Saint-Affrique said that with fewer babies, parents in China have higher expectations on formula makers to invest in science to improve. Still, he expects Danone’s sales — currently skewed more to early life products — to become “more balanced” with medical nutrition catching up in the future.

The CEO also predicted more consolidation in China’s infant milk formula industry, “driven by better quality, better science” to bring value-added products to the market. Though Danone is open to options, the company is more likely to focus on growing sales organically, he added.

title: Beng Kuang’s earnings climb 175% y-o-y to $4.2 mil
article:
Mainboard-listed Beng Kuang Marine has reported patmi of $4.24 million for 3QFY2026 ended Sept 30. This is nearly 175% higher than 3QFY2025, and 87% more than the previous quarter.

The company recorded revenue of $28.6 million, up 10.1% y-o-y, with gross profit margin rising by 210 basis points from 3QFY2025.

Overall, for the first nine months of 2026, patmi stood at $7.78 million, exceeding total earnings for FY2025 which was $5.33 million.

The stronger performance was attributed to offshore lifecycle work and stronger earnings without other gains. For context, the company booked $0.83 million in other gains for 3QFY2025, but this was reversed to other losses of $0.03 million for the current reporting quarter.

The company also recorded the full earnings of Asian Sealand Offshore and Marine this quarter after consolidating the latter into 100% ownership.

Beng Kuang’s offshore lifecycle orderbook stood at $59.8 million as at Sept 30, with a total of $52.6 million delivered in the first nine months of 2026. The shipbuilding orderbook stood at $3.9 million and deck equipment and cranes at $7.5 million.

See also: Elite UK REIT reports 4.8% y-o-y increase in distributable income for 9MFY2026

Shares in Beng Kuang closed unchanged at 33 cents on Nov 2.

title: Estee Lauder raises outlook, buoyed by fragrance demand
article:
(Nov 2): Estee Lauder Cos reported better-than-expected earnings and raised its outlook, the latest sign the beauty conglomerate’s turnaround effort is winning over consumers.

Organic sales will likely grow by 4% to 5.5% in the fiscal year, the company said Monday, more than the prior 3% to 5% estimate. The adjusted earnings per share outlook range was boosted by 10 US cents. The stock rose 3.9% in trading before US exchanges opened.

Demand for fragrances led the growth, helped by the more affordable line Kilian Paris’ Cocktails Collection, which was the company’s fastest-growing brand last quarter.

Estee Lauder said it benefited from efforts to reconnect with its consumer base and appeal to younger spenders.

Diluted earnings per share grew to 64 US cents in the fiscal first quarter, exceeding the 51-cent analyst estimates compiled by Bloomberg. Sales climbed 7% to $3.7 billion.

The New York-based owner of brands such as Le Labo, Tom Ford and La Mer has worked to turn around the business after an extended period of sluggishness coming out of the pandemic. This includes the elimination of 10,000 jobs and an internal restructuring. The updated guidance suggests CEO Stéphane de La Faverie’s strategy is paying off.

See also: LVMH’s China slump threatens hopes for wider luxury recovery

Sales beat estimates in China, where Estee Lauder generated a fifth of its revenue in the latest fiscal year. Company executives are scheduled to hold an event in Shanghai on Wednesday to discuss their strategic plans in the country.

The report underscores that cosmetics spending is on the upswing despite higher inflation in many countries that has eroded purchasing power. In October, French competitor L’Oreal SA reported sales that beat expectations on strong demand for hair products at salons and for premium skincare.

Estee Lauder shares have gained 4.3% this year through last week’s close, short of the 11% advance of the S&P 500 Index over the same period.

See also: Luxury condos seized in Singapore’s biggest money-laundering case find few buyers

The company also launched Glimmer, a high-end fragrance promoted by actress Hailee Steinfeld, last summer, part of its effort to appeal to a younger shopper base.
